description: Shared Markdown memory, bounded session context, source-attributed recall and verified backups for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Shared file-based memory for Codex and Claude Code.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.42.0 adds three optional tools. Recoverable Markdown edit bundles use explicit preview digests, cooperating leases, current source/policy checks and a journal to finish interrupted edits forward. They do not provide multi-file atomic visibility, rollback or a universal power-loss guarantee. A read-only review planner propagates existing direct source-change signals through a caller-declared dependency graph and emits a deterministic bounded worklist; it neither edits notes nor establishes truth. A checkout-only generated-memory lifecycle experiment persists validated authored checksum action memories through production proof/lesson helpers, reopens them in fresh workers and compares bounded adaptive poisoning with selective revocation. Defaults are offline scripted controls. Actual local inference requires an explicitly named model, literal-loopback endpoint and network opt-in. Mock HTTP and scripted controls are not actual-model performance evidence. No new actual-model observation is claimed. Existing optional ontology contracts, exact lookup, structured definition/slot preflight, source-bound routing evaluation, stage interventions, Korean paired observations, source binding, retrieval and revocation retain their previous contracts. No external dataset or upstream implementation is copied. No default hook/configuration change, runtime dependency, company-vault conversion or active installation update is made. Native discovery checks enabled skills and required installed resource bytes, not application compliance or semantic correctness. The seven certificate-bound checker files and committed LF harmless corpus are unchanged from v0.41.0; matching installed bound bytes alone do not require regeneration for this transition. For older changed-byte transitions, reset promoted warnings, align Claude Code/Codex/vault engine versions including rollback, regenerate with harmless replay, then re-promote. Hashes and reports bind bytes and declared observations, not identity, authority or truth. Final release results are recorded only after exact-source verification. For older transitions where checker_sha256 changes: if warnings were promoted to fatal, revert them to warning, bring the Claude Code and Codex installations and a git vault's 00-meta/scripts engine copy to the same version (also when rolling back), regenerate the certificate there, then promote again.
